title.value: Large-Scale Intrinsic Functional Brain Organization Emerges from Three Canonical Spatiotemporal Patterns
title.justification: The title describes the focus of the paper on functional brain organization and its emergence from three spatiotemporal patterns. This directly reflects the core theme of the research.
title.quote: Large-Scale Intrinsic Functional Brain Organization Emerges from Three Canonical Spatiotemporal Patterns

extractions.description: The paper explores the intrinsic functional brain organization through advanced neuroimaging techniques, specifically focusing on how complex brain activities can be reduced to three fundamental spatiotemporal patterns. Through systematic surveys and analysis of resting-state fMRI data, the study identifies and characterizes these patterns, exploring their consistency across different analytic methods and their relation to previously observed phenomena in intrinsic brain activity.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The core subject of the paper is focused on neuroscience, particularly the intrinsic functional organization of the human brain, and does not relate to any aspects of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development directly.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our study conducted a systematic survey of popular analytic techniques and their output on a large sample of resting-state fMRI data.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily discusses neurological patterns and brain function organization, which do not directly relate to any predefined categories of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
primary_category.quote: We found that the apparent complexity of intrinsic functional brain organization can be seamlessly reduced to three fundamental low-frequency spatiotemporal patterns.

secondary_categories.justification: There is no focus on additional topics that intersect with Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development in the context of this paper.
secondary_categories.quote: The temporal dynamics of the three spatiotemporal patterns can be divided into steady-states and propagation events.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not align with the Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development sub-categories since it focuses on brain function rather than environmental topics.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our present study conducted a systematic survey of a host of popular analytic techniques and their output on a large-sample of resting-state fMRI data.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: There is no secondary focus or aspect of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development addressed.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We sought to identify the degree to which the structure of pairwise zero-lag synchronous relationships between BOLD time courses arises from the shared dynamics of the three distinct spatiotemporal patterns.

applications.justification: The applications discussed in the paper pertain to understanding of brain dynamics and functional connectivity and do not involve Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development applications.
applications.quote: Our findings suggest that intrinsic functional brain representations are markedly consistent across analytic methods.

new_primary_category.justification: No new category related to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development is suggested as the paper is centered on neuroscience.
new_primary_category.quote: To date, investigations of these three properties of intrinsic functional brain organization have been largely independent efforts.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Since the focus is on brain functional organization, no new sub-category related to climate or ecological topics is suggested.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We conducted a quantitative survey of widely-used zero-lag functional connectivity (FC) analyses with the primary aim of comparing the spatial overlap between the FC topographies produced by each analysis.
